decisions.reason: The encrypted second channel draws directly on the firm's core cryptography and authentication knowledge and fits its move toward binding mobile communication, so its own R&D can keep improving it, even though it was not visible on the website in 2020–2021.

Mobile PDF signing is close to the established offer and supports the online contract signing direction, but as a narrow feature that was not visible in 2020–2021 it may be folded into the broader identity suite.
The multi-layer end-to-end architecture is the conceptual backbone of the integrated offering and rests most directly on the firm's deep security knowledge, so it is unlikely to be withdrawn.

The email-to-app delivery robot serves a niche use case, the firm has a weak basis for reading its market signals, and its absence from the website since 2019 suggests it has been absorbed into or replaced by the broader secure messaging offer.
App-based authentication is displacing hardware tokens, but the QR token builds on the firm's hardware experience and still serves regulated customers who need offline second factors.
The payment network compliance suite uses the firm's cryptography know-how and meets ongoing regulatory demand, though its compliance-specific scope makes repackaging into other offerings plausible.
